title: Equality, Identity and Indexing
description: Two short checks on list equality versus identity and on tuple indexing. Original to this project.

questions.prompt: after `a = [1, 2]` and `b = a[:]`, which statement is true?
options: `a == b` is True, but `a is b` is False
Both `a == b` and `a is b` are True
`a == b` is False, but `a is b` is True
Both `a == b` and `a is b` are False
questions.correct: `a == b` is True, but `a is b` is False
questions.explanation: Slicing creates a new list with the same contents. Equality compares contents, so a == b is true; identity compares object references, so a is b is false.

questions.prompt: what does this tuple-indexing code print?
questions.explanation: Index 0 selects the first tuple item, 4, while index -1 selects the last item, 9. Negative indexes count backward from the end and do not mutate the tuple.
